title: Seller crisis response quickdeck (iter0)
content:
Overview:
This is a compact, speaker-friendly deck for sellers and SEs to use when a prospect or customer raises an urgent operational/regulatory concern about inference behavior (latency spikes, hallucination/regression, data residency/KMS questions, or suspected data leakage). Designed for fast prep (60–90s skim) before escalation calls. Iter0 = prototyping language and technical checklists.

Slide 1 — Cover / Purpose:
- Title: Seller Crisis Response — Quickdeck (Iter0)
- One-liner: Rapid messaging + handoffs for operational incidents that threaten pilot/contract velocity.
- Use: Before customer calls, internal triage, and post-call handoff.

Slide 2 — Topline seller script (30s):
- Empathize: "I hear you — that matters. We're focused on keeping your app stable and secure."
- Reassure: "We have deterministic fallbacks and a clear incident playbook — I’ll coordinate our ops & SRE immediately."
- Next step: "Can I get a quick read on impact (users, latency, examples)? I’ll loop in engineering and schedule a 1-hour triage."

Speaker note: Keep language simple; avoid product-speak when customers are stressed.

Slide 3 — Common crisis scenarios (quick taxonomy):
1) Latency spike / timeouts at 95th/99th percentile
2) Quality regression / hallucination increase after model update
3) Tokenization or input truncation edge-case causing wrong outputs
4) Data residency or KMS access concern (compliance/regulator escalations)
5) Suspected data leak or unsafe output (security/legal)
6) Capacity shortfall for burst traffic (pilot scaling surprise)

Slide 4 — Rapid diagnosis checklist (what sellers ask on first call):
- When did it start? (timestamp + zone)
- Is it reproducible with example prompts? (collect 2–3 examples)
- Scope: % of users/sessions affected, sample endpoints, model names/versions, route IDs
- Recent changes: model rollouts, config changes (batching/quantization), infra deploys
- Business impact: blocking vs degraded, revenue/time sensitivity

Internal tags to capture (for SEA handoff): impact:low|med|high, showstopper:yes|no, legal_involved:yes|no

Slide 5 — Immediate seller-friendly remedies (non-technical fixes we can propose now):
- Suggest temporary routing to a stable model variant (e.g., previous pinned model)
- Ask customer to reduce max_tokens or sampling temperature for a short window
- Offer to enable stricter input validation/canonicalization in front of calls
- Escalate to Concierge + SRE for a 2-hour response SLA (use when impact=high)

Slide 6 — Technical playbook (for SE handoff):
- Canary rollback: steps to revert traffic to previous model version (PR + rollout flag)
- Routing policy change: move route to dedicated pool or alternate region
- Batching and KV cache flush guidance: when to invalidate caches safely
- Telemetry to collect: per-token latency histogram, model logits variance, trace ids, CPU/GPU sched logs

Quick commands (placeholders to include in final doc):
- Rollback flag: route.set_model(route_id, model: "redwood-v1.2.3")
- Re-route to dedicated pool: routing.move(route_id, pool: "dedicated-usa-east-1")

Slide 7 — Objection playbook (short, ready-to-read answers):
Q: "Why did this start after your update?"
A: "Model updates are A/B rolled with canaries; sometimes edge prompts show regressions — our rollback and telemetry help provide immediate mitigation while we debug."

Q: "Can you guarantee no data left the region?"
A: "We respect pinned residency and can provide audit logs; if needed we’ll escalate to our security team for formal attestation and KMS checks."

Q: "What is the impact on cost if we use dedicated?"
A: "Dedicated provides predictability — we’ll map expected per-1000-token units and show cost delta vs hosted with burst. Quick model: $X per 1M tokens on hosted vs $Y reserved for capacity."

Slide 8 — Evidence & trust signals (snippets sellers can use):
- 99.9% uptime SLA on Dedicated (when purchased) — link to SLA page (post-launch)
- Case snippet: "Retail search pilot — rolled back v2.1 after quality dip, route pin restored baseline in 45 mins"
- Audit logs: we can export KMS/HSM access events within 24 hours on request

Slide 9 — Seller play checklist (pre-call 60s):
- Grab model name/version and route ID from customer
- Ask for 2–3 example prompts and timestamps
- Confirm whether legal/regulatory is on the thread
- Offer 30/60/120 minute response SLAs depending on impact
- Promise a named follow-up owner (SE + SRE contact)

Slide 10 — Handoff template (paste into Slack / email):
- Subject: URGENT | {account} | {issue short}
- Body: {one-line impact}, model={model}, route={route}, examples={example1; example2}, start={ts}, severity={low|med|high}, requested response SLA={60m/120m}
- Tag: #ops-triage and ping @oncall-sre

Slide 11 — Escalation matrix & contact points (who to call):
- Level 1: SE on duty (day shift) — internal Slack handle
- Level 2: Infra SRE oncall — JIRA: JIRA-ENG-9876 (triage playbook)
- Level 3: Security/Legal contact (for compliance/data leakage) — escalate with "Legal Escalation" template in Confluence

Slide 12 — Open questions / backlog for product & docs:
- Formalize the cost delta calculator for dedicated vs hosted for use in sales decks (owner: Marcus)
- Add canned rollback commands to Console quick-actions (owner: infra team)
- Define templated evidence exports (audit + telemetry) with <24h SLA (owner: security)

Appendix — Notes to self (rough):
- Prototype should be one sheet printable A4 for sellers to keep on calls.
- Replace placeholders with real cost numbers before next seller training on 2026-03-15.
- Link to related playbooks: CONFLUENCE-12345 (ops), https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/42 (draft runbook).

TODOs before internal preview:
- Dana: add concrete rollback CLI and console screenshots
- Priya: draft one customer case snippet and legal-safe wording
- Marcus: build the quick pricing delta table (hosted vs dedicated)

Last edited notes:
- Kept deliberately minimal technical detail for seller comfort. SEs can use the handed-off technical playbook in the next doc.
- This is a living deck — expect rapid iteration after first adoption in pilot accounts.
